question.text: What is the role of an 'Authorized Person' in ETIRD trading?

answer.text: A person appointed by a stock broker who is not an exchange member but can introduce clients and facilitate orders on behalf of the broker
A person authorized by SEBI to trade directly on the exchange
An exchange employee who monitors compliance
A clearing corporation official who approves large orders

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series IV (pp.195, 294), an Authorized Person (AP) is appointed by a stock broker and acts as the broker's agent for exchange trading access. APs are not exchange members; they require exchange approval and operate under a written trading-member/AP agreement. The Trap: APs do not trade directly on the exchange in their own right, and they are not exchange or clearing-corporation employees. They also do not carry their own SEBI registration — they operate through the appointing broker under exchange approval and the TM-AP agreement. Note: Client funds and securities must flow directly between the client and the broker — never through the AP.
